chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from 'Abbad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man whom the Imam paused for the *li'an* (cursing), so he testified with two testimonies, then hesitated/backed down, so he belied himself before he was finished with the *li'an*. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the penalty (*hadd*) of the slanderer, and there is no separation between him and his wife.'

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: The penalty of the slanderer, referring to the flogging prescribed for those who accuse others of adultery without proof
key_terms.شَهَادَتَيْنِ: Two testimonies, referring to the four oaths (two for each party) required in the li'an procedure
key_terms.لِلِّعَانِ: Li'an (cursing), a specific judicial procedure for divorce based on mutual oaths and curses
key_terms.نَكَلَ: He hesitated or backed down, indicating retraction or failure to complete the procedure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband retracts his testimony during the li'an process before it is finished?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the procedural integrity of *li'an* by establishing that premature retraction of testimony invalidates the divorce, thereby preserving the marital bond while imposing the *hadd* penalty for slander. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the finality of the oath-taking phase, distinguishing between mere accusation and the completed legal act of separation. This ruling underscores the gravity of *li'an* as a distinct mechanism for resolving unproven adultery accusations within the family structure.
